providers.name: Xfinity
providers.policy: Comcast gives a pro rata credit for a service interruption that lasts more than 24 consecutive hours after you report it, capped at that month's fixed charges for the service. Xfinity also applies outage credits automatically when your account is eligible, up to a maximum credit limit.
providers.deadline: Request the pro rata credit within 120 days of the service interruption.
providers.howTo: Sign in at xfinity.com or in the Xfinity app, open Support, scroll to Outage map and credit and tap Check credit eligibility, or ask Xfinity Assistant for a credit and choose service outage as the reason.
providers.note: The agreement adds shorter TV-only rules in some states: four hours in New York and Ohio, six hours in New Jersey and Maine, and an automatic credit after 24 hours in Connecticut.

providers.name: Xfinity Mobile
providers.policy: The Xfinity Mobile customer agreement does not promise a credit for service interruptions; it says you may dispute a charge or request a billing credit within 120 days of the billing statement date, and credits are decided case by case.
providers.deadline: Request a billing credit within 120 days of the bill date; after that you waive the right to the credit.
providers.howTo: Contact Xfinity Mobile support through chat in the Xfinity app or at xfinity.com and ask for a billing credit for the outage.
providers.note: The agreement states that cellular service availability is not guaranteed.

providers.name: AT&T
providers.policy: Under the AT&T Guarantee, AT&T Internet Air customers get a bill credit for downtime lasting 20 minutes or more; restrictions and exclusions apply. The Guarantee terms make the benefit the exclusive remedy, let AT&T change or cancel the program at any time, and say that where a law requires a larger outage benefit AT&T provides only the legally required one.
providers.howTo: AT&T emails eligible customers after a qualifying outage; if you did not get an email, contact AT&T support and ask about the AT&T Guarantee outage credit.
providers.note: AT&T's business support page lists the thresholds as 20 minutes for fiber and 60 minutes for a wireless outage caused by one incident hitting 8 or more towers; the consumer Fiber and wireless thresholds could not be verified on a page that loaded.

providers.name: Verizon Fios
providers.policy: For a Fios TV outage Verizon says you may be entitled to a service credit, typically a prorated amount of your current monthly bill, and in most cases you must promptly report the outage to qualify. The Fios Internet terms in the Fios Customer Agreement do not state an outage credit, so an internet credit is handled case by case.
providers.howTo: Report the outage to Verizon as soon as it happens, then ask Verizon support for the credit by phone or chat.
providers.note: New Jersey section of the notice: a TV outage of 6 to 24 hours earns a one-day credit and a longer outage a credit per day; request it within 30 days of the outage.

providers.name: Verizon
providers.policy: If you are a postpaid customer, lose service in your coverage area for more than 24 hours in a row, and Verizon is at fault, Verizon gives you a credit for the time lost.
providers.howTo: Call Verizon at 800-922-0204, or use the contact form or 24/7 chat linked from the network outage FAQ page, and ask for the credit.
providers.note: A network outage is not the same as no coverage or a weak signal; those do not qualify.

providers.name: Optimum
providers.policy: If a cable-related outage lasts more than four consecutive hours, Optimum gives full credit on your bill for the time lost, provided you contact Optimum within 30 days of the outage.
providers.deadline: Contact Optimum within 30 days of the outage.
providers.howTo: Chat with Optimum at optimum.net/support, use the My Optimum app, or call Optimum support and ask for the outage credit.
providers.note: The page describes cable-related outages; it does not say whether internet or phone outages get the same credit.

providers.name: Frontier
providers.policy: Frontier's residential internet terms say Frontier reserves the right to refuse refunds, offsets and credit allowances for interruptions of service, so any outage credit is case by case.
providers.howTo: Report the outage and ask Frontier support for a credit; granting it is at Frontier's discretion.
providers.note: Terms last updated March 2023; the newer copy on frontier.com could not be fetched for verification.

providers.name: Quantum Fiber / CenturyLink
providers.policy: Quantum Fiber handles outage credits on request: if you experienced an outage and would like a credit, contact support and they can help.
providers.howTo: Call 833-250-6306 (7 days a week, 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. Central) or use the chat bubble on the Quantum Fiber website or app and ask for an outage credit.
providers.note: CenturyLink's own Credit for No Service help page could not be fetched for verification.

providers.name: Google Fiber
providers.policy: gFiber proactively credits your account for qualified service disruptions where applicable; you do not need to call or submit a request. The credit appears as a separate line item under Previous Payments & Credits on your next monthly statement.
providers.howTo: Nothing to file: check the Previous Payments & Credits section of your next gFiber bill, and contact gFiber support if a credit is missing.

providers.name: Astound Broadband
providers.policy: Astound's customer terms say that, subject to applicable law, credit will be given for qualifying outages; the terms do not define a qualifying outage or a minimum length.
providers.howTo: Report the outage and ask for the credit by calling 1-800-427-8686 (24/7), using Live Chat on astound.com, or through the MyAstound app.
providers.note: Billing disputes must be raised within 180 days of the invoice date.

providers.name: Kinetic by Windstream
providers.policy: Kinetic's policy is to issue a credit, upon request, for service interruptions longer than 24 hours. No credit is issued if Kinetic was not notified promptly or for situations beyond its control.
providers.howTo: Report the outage right away through the Go Kinetic portal or app or by calling 1-800-347-1991 (24/7), then ask for the credit.

providers.name: Visible
providers.policy: If you lose service for more than 24 hours in a row and Visible is at fault, Visible gives you a credit for the time lost; the terms call this your only right for interrupted service.
providers.howTo: Chat with Visible Customer Care in the Visible app or at visible.com and ask for the credit.

providers.name: Cricket Wireless
providers.policy: If your wireless service is interrupted for 24 or more continuous hours by a cause within Cricket's control, Cricket issues, upon request, an account credit equal to a pro-rata adjustment of the monthly service fee for the time service was unavailable, not to exceed the monthly fee.
providers.howTo: Call Customer Care at 1-800-274-2538 or dial 611 from your Cricket phone, or use chat on the Cricket support site, and ask for the outage credit.
providers.note: Terms revised October 1, 2026; the credit is Cricket's only liability for service failures.

providers.name: Boost Mobile
providers.policy: Boost's terms do not promise a credit for outages: Boost says it is not responsible for interruptions, delays or limitations of service, and its total liability is limited to service credits of up to $500. Any outage credit is at Boost's discretion.
providers.howTo: Chat with Boost (daily 8 a.m. to midnight ET) or call Customer Care at 833-502-6678 and ask whether a credit is available for the outage.

providers.name: Consumer Cellular
providers.policy: If your service is interrupted for 24 or more continuous hours by a cause within Consumer Cellular's control, it issues, upon request, a credit equal to a prorated adjustment of the monthly service charges for the time service was unavailable, not to exceed the monthly fees.
providers.howTo: Contact Consumer Cellular customer support and ask for the prorated credit; it is only issued on request.
providers.note: Wireless Customer Agreement dated June 25, 2025; the credit is Consumer Cellular's only liability for service failures.

rules.title: New York cable outage credits
rules.text: Cable TV companies must credit a subscriber for an outage not caused by the subscriber that lasts more than 4 continuous hours, counted from when the company first becomes aware of it. The credit is pro-rated by the days of the outage and is never less than 24 hours' credit; the subscriber must ask for it, by phone or in writing, within 90 days of the outage.

rules.title: New York storm outage credits for phone and cable
rules.text: Since 2023, when a storm or power outage takes down telephone or cable service for 100 or more subscribers, major telephone and cable companies must credit residential customers 1/30th of the monthly rate for each 24 hours, or part of one, that service is out for 24 hours or more. For an interruption under 24 hours, a one-day credit is issued if the subscriber requests it because service that day was substantially impaired; if loss of commercial power contributed, the credit period starts 24 hours after power is restored.

rules.title: New Jersey cable outage credits
rules.text: New Jersey's cable television rules (N.J.A.C. 14:18-3.5) require cable TV operators to credit customers for service outages, and a 2024 Board of Public Utilities order with Altice (Optimum) reaffirms that duty. The rule's hour thresholds could not be verified on a state page; ask your cable company for the outage credit and cite N.J.A.C. 14:18-3.5.

rules.title: Rhode Island cable outage credits
rules.text: If cable service is interrupted for more than 24 hours for any reason other than the subscriber's negligence, and the interruption is reported to the company, the subscriber gets a prorated credit on the monthly service charge for each 24-hour period, or fraction of one, that the interruption continues. No credit is given for interruptions under 24 hours, and every month counts as 30 days for the proration (815-RICR-10-05-1, section 1.13.9(D)).

rules.title: Maine cable and video outage credits
rules.text: If service to a subscriber is interrupted for 6 or more consecutive hours in a 30-day period, the franchisee must, upon request, grant that subscriber a pro rata credit or rebate (30-A M.R.S. section 3010(1)(A)).
